_why: OD-52. rules.json gives every rule in this design a stable id; this file says WHICH BUILD ITEM owns each one. The mapping is by section, because a section is where a rule lives and a build item is what implements that section. It is authored deliberately, not inferred: a wrong row here puts a rule on the wrong engineer's desk, which is exactly the failure the id scheme exists to prevent. Check D19 reads the CARDS, not this file — this file only generates their `Rules implemented` blocks, so a card can be corrected by hand and the gate will believe the card.

_unclaimed_sections.5.6: A standing constraint on HOW we work (no language model in the phase-1 pipeline), not a thing any build item constructs. OD-52 allows this, provided it is declared rather than silent.
_unclaimed_sections.7.1: The build sequence describes the items themselves; a rule about the order of the work is not implemented BY one of the items in it.
_unclaimed_sections.7.3: The honest list of what the author is unsure about. These become rules only once they are answered, and then they land in the section that answers them.
_unclaimed_sections.7.5: The deployment and branching policy. It is enforced by the release process and by `.claude/rules/branching-model.md`, not by application code.
